| | |
|---|---|
| **Software version** | 4.0.2 |
| **Spec revision** | v001 |
| **Date** | 2026-07-22 |
| **Status** | Implemented |

## Problem

When TabMaster AI loads, every browser window gets a default display name
generated from alphabetical adjective/noun word lists: "Able Ant", "Blue Bear",
"Calm Cat", and so on (A, B, C… ordering, cycling through five words per
letter).

These names are whimsical but unhelpful: they carry no information about a
window's position or identity, and users must mentally map arbitrary word pairs
to windows. Sequential names are easier to scan and to talk about ("close
window3").

## Change

Default window names become sequential: `window1`, `window2`, `window3`, …
assigned in the order windows are reported by the browser (the same index
ordering the old scheme used).

### Behavior details

- `generateWindowName(index)` returns `window{index + 1}` (1-based, no
  padding, no space).
- `generateWindowNames(windowIds)` is unchanged in shape: it maps each window
  ID to its generated name by input order.
- **Custom names still win.** Names the user typed, and names produced by the
  AI "Auto Name" feature, are stored as `customWindowNames` and continue to
  override the generated defaults at merge time in `App.tsx` (`loadTabs`).
  This spec changes only the fallback default.
- Windows are not renamed at the browser level; as before, this is a display
  name inside the extension.

### Code cleanup

`services/nameGenerator.ts` shrinks from ~97 lines to ~18: the `ADJECTIVES`
and `NOUNS` word tables (52 lists, 260 words) and the alphabet-cycling logic
are deleted. No other module imported them.

## Affected files

- `services/nameGenerator.ts` — rewritten (word lists removed, sequential
  logic added).

Call sites in `App.tsx` are untouched; the function signatures are preserved.

## Out of scope

- AI-generated window naming (`generateWindowNamesWithAI` in
  `services/geminiService.ts`) is unchanged.
- Renumbering after windows close (e.g. gaps like window1, window3) follows
  the same rule as the old scheme: defaults are recomputed from current window
  order on each load, so numbers stay contiguous.
